brief.data: Spring pool: $186,500 from the student activity fee. 64 club requests totaling $271,930. Each request: club name, line items (travel, event, equipment, food), amount requested, committee-approved amount, vote tally (e.g., 5–1–1), notes from deliberation, policy flags (e.g., 'food >25% of request', 'off-campus travel requires risk form'). Rescission rules: written reason required, 10-day appeal window, appeals go to the full Senate. Advisor Carla Ruiz's review status: 'Reviewed, 2 comments'. Spending opens Dec 1.

prompt:
I need the front end for Fundfloor. Budget allocation software for university student governments, where the student finance committee commits funding from the student activity fee to registered clubs and handles appeals and rescinded awards.

Who's using it: Jordan Mbeki, a junior majoring in public policy and the elected treasurer of the Associated Students at a public university of 19,000 students. Jordan chairs the seven-member finance committee and is the only person who can finalize allocations; a staff advisor from the Office of Student Life reviews but doesn't vote.

What they're doing right now: The committee voted Thursday night on spring allocations, and Jordan is now committing the results so clubs can see their awards and start spending on Dec 1. The approved total is $3,800 over the remaining pool, because the committee approved a late amendment for the Robotics Club's competition travel. Jordan has to decide which pending awards to trim or defer before committing, knowing that once awards are committed, clubs get notified and any reduction later becomes a formal rescission that clubs can appeal within 10 days. One award, to the Esports Club, was already committed by mistake last week at $2,400 instead of $1,400 and needs to be walked back.

What's in the system at this point: Spring pool: $186,500 from the student activity fee. 64 club requests totaling $271,930. Each request: club name, line items (travel, event, equipment, food), amount requested, committee-approved amount, vote tally (e.g., 5–1–1), notes from deliberation, policy flags (e.g., 'food >25% of request', 'off-campus travel requires risk form'). Current state: 58 approved pending commit ($190,300), 4 denied, 2 tabled until January. Robotics Club late amendment: +$6,200 for regional competition in Dayton. Esports Club award committed Nov 9 at $2,400 (approved amount $1,400), club already notified, $0 spent so far. Rescission rules: written reason required, 10-day appeal window, appeals go to the full Senate. Advisor Carla Ruiz's review status: 'Reviewed, 2 comments'. Spending opens Dec 1.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
